author: Samuil Petkov
new_mathematical_refinements: The phase-resolved deterministic error is now quantified as `O(log log n / log n)`, with a phase-independent constant, in a proved remark. The unnormalized remainder is `O(n log log n / (log n)^4)`. The prior-work comparison is more precise, a few formal-proof-management phrases have been simplified, and Appendix B starts with its opening proof. The fixed uniform coefficient and abstract are unchanged. Corollary 11.2 also gives a phase-independent failure-probability bound O((log n)^(2/log 2+1/2)/n) for the same remainder order, and for the fixed-coefficient consequence after an increased threshold. Its proof uses the existing explicit tail amplification and sums all four exceptional-event bounds.
formalization_scope: Appendix H distinguishes the released full-sequence fixed-coefficient theorem and its tail-amplification route from the phase refinement and the complete written mean-positive-excess proof. The quantified remainder and failure-probability bound belong to the written refinement; neither is claimed as a newly released Lean theorem.

second_review.scope: Focused technical, boundary, and documentation review after the previous improvements; no major rewrite.
second_review.result: No new blocking mathematical issue found in the reviewed material.
second_review.changes: Lemma 10.1 now states the existing exp(-c sqrt n) exceptional-probability bound explicitly and displays its exact density union bound. The greedy construction explicitly uses integrality at ceil(n^(1/4)); its independent-set-size constant is separated from the tail constant. Appendix C and Corollary 11.2 cite the quantitative lemma directly. The main theorem, leading coefficient, remainder order, and failure-probability rate are unchanged.

third_review.scope: One further focused mathematical and prose pass; preserve structure and accepted Lean sources.
third_review.result: No new blocking mathematical issue found in the reviewed material.
third_review.changes: Corollary 11.2 retains the rounding-phase factor in the failure bound: O(w_n), with beta=2/log(2)+1/2 and w_n=((log n)^beta/n)((log n)/n)^(1-delta_n). Constants and the eventual threshold remain phase-independent. For each fixed eta in (0,1), failure is O(n^(-1-eta)(log n)^(beta+eta)) along integers satisfying delta_n<=1-eta. The proof retains the phase term in the first-moment exponent and absorbs all four exceptional terms. The main theorem, fixed leading coefficient, and remainder order are unchanged.

current_failure_probability: O(((log n)^beta/n)((log n)/n)^(1-delta_n)), beta=2/log(2)+1/2; phase-independent constants
